subject: Fraktal Labs trial: implementation plan & POC milestones
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kwan <sara@fraktal.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fraktal Labs trial: implementation plan & POC milestones

Thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning, Sara — good to meet the Fraktal team. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the proposed POC scope, success criteria, timeline, and a concise integration playbook so your engineers have what they need to start planning. I attached a simple milestones spreadsheet and an API map PDF for reference.

POC goal (30-day trial): Validate a streaming assistant for internal invoices lookup and triage that reduces manual search time and surface accuracy of returned vendor matches to >= 85% on sample dataset.

Success criteria (we agreed on):
1) Functional: End-to-end integration demonstrating streaming responses for the invoice triage flow with model-assisted extraction (vendor, amount, date) and tool-calling to your search service.
2) Quality: Precision of vendor match >= 85% on the 2k-sample test set; end-to-end user satisfaction >= 4/5 from 5 pilot users.
3) Performance: 95th percentile latency for a streaming single-turn query < 450ms after initial token warm-up; stable throughput of 120 reqs/min for concurrent pilot usage.
4) Observability: Instrumentation for token usage, per-request latency, and error traces available to both teams.

Proposed timeline (can shift by a week if needed):
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff + security questionnaire start.
- Week 1: SDK integration + streaming demo (sample data ingestion).
- Week 2: Test harness + quality tuning (prompt sets and evals).
- Week 3: Pilot with 5 internal users + metrics review.
- Week 4: Acceptance review and next steps (scale / pricing).

Integration highlights (technical):
- SDKs: We provide Node and Python SDKs. Key methods: redwood.client.streamConversation({model, route, sessionId, callbacks}) and redwood.client.callTool({tool, input}).
- API routes: POST /v1/generate for non-streaming; WebSocket /v1/stream for streaming token deltas with incremental 'delta' frames; tool-calls invoked via structured function JSON in the stream with a final call_confirmation event.
- Streaming semantics: initial response arrives <150ms for short prompts; incremental frames include partial text + token index and optional tooling requests. Client should be prepared to apply prefix caching across repeated invoice prefixes.
- Tool calling: Example: send {"tool":"fraktal_search.v1.lookup","args":{"vendor_query":"Acme LLC","top_k":5}}; the platform returns tool results as canonical JSON before model continues.
- KV / cache: Recommend enabling prefix KV cache for repeated vendor name lookups to cut cost by ~30% during the pilot.
- Quantization / perf: For highest throughput, we suggest the 4-bit int8-quant profile on dedicated capacity; hosted default will also be fine for this POC but expect ~10–15% higher latency.

Owners & asks:
- Fraktal: Provide a small sample dataset (2k anonymized invoices) and a contact for your infra (eng+fraktal@fraktal.ai).
- Redwood: Ben (cc) will own the SDK integration support and demo; Marissa will run pilot logistics and user feedback collection. I'll own overall milestone tracking and the acceptance review.

Immediate next steps:
1) Sara: confirm sample data delivery timing and any data access constraints (S3 link or shared Drive).
2) Fraktal infra: let us know any firewall / egress restrictions so we can share IP allowlist.
3) Redwood: we start a short integration session (30–45m) with your engineers — proposed Monday at 10am PT.

Thanks — attaching milestone sheet. If those timelines work, I’ll lock the kickoff.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143

On Fri, 05 Jul 2028 at 09:12, Rishi Malhotra wrote:
> Integration highlights (technical):

Hi Sara — quick technical clarifications and a couple implementation tips for your eng team before the kickoff.

1) SDK pairing: If you use our Node SDK, the minimal flow for streaming looks like:

const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY});
const stream = client.streamConversation({model: 'redwood-stream-1', route: 'invoice-triage', sessionId: 'fraktal-dev-01'});
stream.on('delta', d => process.stdout.write(d.text));
stream.on('tool', t => handleToolCall(t));
stream.start({input: 'Find vendor for invoice #1024'});

2) WebSocket handshake requires a short-lived token we provide on request; if you prefer inbound-only streaming we can open an outbound connection from your side (we'll give a small nginx config snippet).

3) For tool-calling: send structured function definitions in the initial call (name + argSchema). Our platform will emit a call request mid-stream if the model decides to use it. Example call payload we recommend: {name: 'fraktal_search.v1.lookup', args: {query: 'Acme', max_results: 5}}. Handle the returned JSON, then ACK to the stream to let the model continue.

4) Rate-limits and quotas: during the POC we’ll set a soft limit of 200 RPM with burst to 400 for testing. If you need higher, we can shift to a dedicated slot during Week 3.

5) Debugging: enable full request/response capture for your first 100 calls (we’ll mask tokens) so we can quickly diagnose prompt/parse issues.

I’ll be on the kickoff; I can prepare a 15-minute live coding demo to exercise the tool-calling path.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
